applicability_conditions: Apply only when the task asks for a binary Yes/No judgment about whether a specified factor caused or intentionally produced an outcome.
Apply the causal-attribution guidance only when the question is about causation rather than intentionality.
Apply the intentionality guidance only when the question asks whether an outcome was intentionally produced.

failure_taxonomy.description: Core-only responses provided explanations or punctuation instead of exactly one allowed label, causing exact-match parse failures.
Core-only responses treated a broad background condition or passive standing condition as causal merely because it was part of the chain leading to the outcome.
Development items show that when a later independent action or event directly produces the outcome, earlier background or enabling factors should not automatically be labeled as causes.

adapter_text:
For this task, output exactly one token: Yes or No. Do not include punctuation, qualifiers, or explanation.

For causal-attribution questions: answer Yes only when the specified factor is the direct/proximate or normatively salient producer of the outcome. Answer No when the specified factor is merely a broad background condition, passive standing condition, or incidental enabling link, especially when a later independent action or event directly produces the outcome. Do not answer Yes solely because the factor is part of a but-for chain.

For intentionality questions, make the intentionality judgment using the Core Skill, while preserving the exact Yes/No-only output format.
fallback_policy: Outside binary causal-attribution or intentionality questions with the required Yes/No output contract, use Core-only behavior and do not apply these causal-attribution heuristics.
changes_from_previous: Retained the exact-output rule associated with resolving all observed parse failures.
Retained the proximate/normatively salient causation rule associated with observed causal-attribution errors.
Narrowed the list of non-causal factors by removing unsupported examples not needed for the observed recurring mechanism.
predicted_regression_risks: The proximate-cause heuristic could underpredict Yes in cases where the task expects attribution to a background factor despite an intervening event.
The passive-standing-condition rule could underpredict Yes in cases where simultaneous standing conditions are treated as jointly causal by the dataset.
evidence_limitations: Only three development items are available.
Development evidence covers only the causal_attribution subgroup; intentionality behavior is constrained only by the output contract.
No holdout data or holdout results were used.
